book.author: Frank W. J. Olver
book.title: Asymptotics and Special Functions
book.edition: Corrected 1997 A K Peters edition; PDF imprint also records the CRC 2010 reprint
book.page_convention: PDF page = printed Arabic page + 19; critical formula pages were visually checked because the embedded OCR misreads digits and omits formulas.

scope: Source-to-admission proof-route review at the recorded 983-admission baseline; subsequent implementation is recorded separately below.

groups.proof_detail: Detailed successive-approximation proof and endpoint arguments; the x+log x example is worked in section 3.6, p.200.
groups.lean_route: Extend the proved tail-integral Volterra result to finite intervals and both orientations; majorize successive differences by integrated powers divided by factorials. Derive derivative bounds, normalized endpoint limits, and dominant solutions. For the example retain an integration constant that normalizes the leading factor.
remaining_formalization: Finite-endpoint Volterra existence and differentiation
Uniqueness of the normalized recessive solution and extension of the dominant solution
Example requires extending solutions from a positive-f tail to the full interval (0,infinity)

targets.statement_correction: Approved and applied: integrability for every x ≥ x₀; proof remains admitted.
Approved and applied: integrability for every x ≥ x₀; proof remains admitted.

groups.proof_detail: Detailed proof. The text explicitly permits merely asymptotic, nonconvergent local series.
groups.lean_route: Split the integral near its endpoint; substitute v=p(t)-p(a); revert the local expansion and identify q/p-prime coefficients with laplaceCoeff; apply the proved Watson lemma. Bound the far tail by a strictly positive phase gap and the existing integrable majorant.
remaining_formalization: General real-asymptotic reversion with the project coefficient normalization
One-dimensional change of variables on a sufficiently small monotonic interval
Exponential tail estimate with arbitrary integrable amplitude

groups.proof_detail: Detailed contour-change and Watson argument, with branch choices and path conditions.
groups.lean_route: Use the analytic local inverse of v=p(t)-p(a), track the logarithmic powers on the chosen path, apply rotated Watson estimates and split the two sides of a simple saddle.
remaining_formalization: Local inverse and coefficient bridge
Uniform contour-tail bounds
Consistent continuous arguments and the two saddle branches
groups.priority: After real Laplace and coefficient bridge

groups.topic: Endpoint stationary phase and oscillatory Watson
groups.proof_detail: Proofs and preliminary lemmas; the all-order extension is explained in section 14.
groups.lean_route: Separate the endpoint singular model from the smooth tail. Use repeated integration by parts on the tail and scaled oscillatory Gamma integrals on the endpoint model; pass to improper limits with the stated tail hypotheses.
remaining_formalization: All-order oscillatory endpoint remainder estimate
Tail estimates for the exact finite- and infinite-endpoint hypotheses

groups.topic: Singular Darboux and Legendre coefficient asymptotics
groups.proof_detail: Boundary-Fourier proof outline and a worked Legendre example; singular-boundary details still need formalization.
groups.lean_route: Prove integrable boundary traces and radial convergence for finitely many algebraic singularities. Apply Riemann-Lebesgue and integration by parts. For Legendre subtract the existing comparison function, whose local residual is constant plus O(distance^(1/2)); use m=1 and the Gamma-ratio asymptotic.
remaining_formalization: Uniform integrability of radial traces near finitely many boundary points
Periodic boundary integration by parts with integrable singular derivatives
Principal-branch residual estimates at exp(+/-i alpha)

groups.proof_detail: Explicit Cauchy-majorant convergence proof, reduction-of-order construction, and a parameter-limit alternative.
groups.lean_route: Bound the coefficient recurrence using Cauchy estimates on every smaller circle and a positive scalar majorant. For the resonant solution integrate z^(-N-1) times an analytic factor; its z^N coefficient produces the logarithm. Adjust by a multiple of the first solution to match the project normalization.
remaining_formalization: Majorant proof for the full stated convergence radius
Logarithmic series and normalization at resonant indices
Independence and continuation across zeros of the first solution

groups.topic: Rank-one irregular solutions and Stokes connections
groups.proof_detail: Explicit remainder integral equation, successive-approximation proof, and rotated-solution connection argument.
groups.lean_route: Insert a truncated formal solution, solve the residual equation by a Volterra construction on progressive paths, and use recessivity to identify the same normalized solution for every truncation order. Compare rotated fundamental solutions to obtain the connection constants.
remaining_formalization: Complex progressive-path integral equation
Holomorphic continuation on the logarithmic plane
Uniform sector bounds and normalized recessive uniqueness

groups.proof_detail: Explicit error integral equation and proof outline using Chapter 6 Theorem 10.1; modulus/weight estimates occur earlier in the chapter.
groups.lean_route: Use the Airy pair and its Wronskian to form the Green kernel. Prove weighted kernel and derivative bounds, solve the forced error equation, then use section 7.4 to split the envelope error into bounded Ai/Ai-prime or Bi/Bi-prime components. Olver has W1 of Bi type and W2 of Ai type: swap labels; use Olver n = Lean n-1.
remaining_formalization: Weighted Airy Green-kernel bounds
Finite-interval weighted Volterra theorem
Bridge between Olver E,M,N weights and project envelopes
Use positive envelopes rather than dividing by Ai or Ai-prime at their zeros.

groups.proof_detail: Explicit I/K Green-kernel proof; the J/Y case is developed with modulus bounds and the same integral-equation theorem.
groups.lean_route: Use the I/K and J/Y fundamental pairs with their Wronskians, normalize the kernels as in section 3.2, and control the error by weighted variations of sqrt(abs(xi))*B. Convert the result to the project compound expansions; use Olver n = Lean n-1.
remaining_formalization: Weighted Bessel kernel and derivative estimates uniform near zero
Oscillatory modulus/envelope comparison
Positive and negative orientations with consistent normalizations
groups.priority: After weighted Volterra; supports Legendre applications

groups.proof_detail: Outline of the uniform method, followed by a detailed worked error-bound argument.
groups.lean_route: Integrate the uniform amplitude remainder against the positive Gaussian weight, rescale tau=sqrt(x)*w, and estimate the discarded upper tail uniformly using the gap kappa-a2>0. Retain the exact project centered moments and coefficient convention.
remaining_formalization: Weighted-moment integrability and uniform tail comparison
Bounds on the finite polynomial part from the supplied uniform remainder hypotheses
groups.priority: Focused integral estimate after checking exact uniform hypotheses

groups.topic: Nicholson integral for squared Bessel functions
groups.proof_detail: A full proof: the integral satisfies the third-order equation for products of Bessel solutions, and large-argument asymptotics fix its three constants.
groups.lean_route: Prove convergence and differentiation under the integral, derive the third-order product equation, establish a product-solution basis, and identify the constants using the real positive large-argument limit. Retain all complex orders in the project statement.
remaining_formalization: Dominated derivative bounds near zero and infinity
Third-order product-ODE basis/uniqueness
Uniform asymptotics to exclude residual oscillatory Hankel-square terms
groups.priority: A direct source, but a substantial dedicated proof

recommended_order: Singular Darboux and finite-interval Liouville-Green extensions
Real Laplace and its coefficient-reversion bridge
Weighted Airy/Bessel Green-kernel Volterra theorem and the five model templates

secondary_candidates.caution: Use the Bessel model plus a separate normalization/ODE transformation. Do not claim all simultaneous large-degree/order regimes follow from the fixed-order examples.

sources: Chapter 11 sections 3-7, turning-point and zero methods
secondary_candidates.caution: The worked Chapter 6 example treats a large positive cylinder parameter and supplies a leading approximation. Remaining negative-parameter, all-order and turning-point statements need separate transformations, full DLMF normalizers, coefficient identities and zero enumeration; this is not a promise to close all 17 admissions.
The single combined project statement includes real and complex families and all printed coefficients; real-zero asymptotics alone are insufficient.
Need the exact improper-tail and coefficient-identification bridges, not just an existence assertion for an expansion.

coverage_limits: The 1997 volume reprints the 1974 text with corrections, rather than rewriting every chapter to cover subsequent research.
No matching complete treatment was found for the Chapter 2 distributional-asymptotics block, general difference-equation asymptotics, or every modern hyperasymptotic/late-coefficient statement.
Mathieu appears as an exercise/application; the book does not supply direct proofs for all 118 remaining Mathieu admissions.
No direct proof source was identified for the main Painleve, matrix-argument, combinatorial or number-theoretic blocks.

validation.upstream_check: Mathlib and pinned TauCeti ODE/asymptotic APIs and local support were inspected. TauCeti Analysis/ODE/Frobenius is the integrability theorem, not the Fuchs-Frobenius regular-singular power-series theorem.
